title: Cache gateway bootstrap config and avoid default-only config writes
content: Updated memcli gateway bootstrap to cache resolved gateway config at module scope so URL/token lookups do not reread files on every call. Also changed persistence logic so ~/.memspren-config is only written when real values are discovered from env or ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json, avoiding writes driven solely by the default loopback URL.

title: Restore gateway bootstrap in canonical openclaw/scripts memcli
content: Reapplied the .memspren-config / ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json gateway bootstrap logic into the canonical openclaw/scripts/memcli package after repo cleanup, ensuring the main MemSpren package no longer relies on environment-only gateway auth.

title: Consolidate memcli packaging to openclaw/scripts
content: Removed the redundant top-level scripts tree and made openclaw/scripts/memcli the canonical packaging source. Updated setuptools package discovery, pytest paths, and colocated prompts/schemas under the packaged memcli tree to eliminate drift between the skill copy and the main repo.

title: Bootstrap OpenClaw gateway credentials into .memspren-config
content: Updated memcli to read gateway URL/token from ~/.memspren-config first, and bootstrap missing values from ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json (with environment override precedence). Setup now seeds the config automatically so installed memcli runs do not depend on shell rc files for Gateway authentication.

title: Move MemSpren prompts and schemas under package for installed CLI
content: Moved prompts and schemas into the memcli package and updated package-data entries to include package-local assets. This fixes installed memcli runs that could not find extraction prompts/schemas after switching workflows to use the memcli console script.

title: Package MemSpren prompts and schemas for installed memcli runs
content: Updated MemSpren packaging so installed memcli runs can resolve prompt and schema assets outside repo-local execution. Added package-data entries for prompts/schemas and updated memcli path resolution to prefer packaged resources with repo fallback, fixing sync failures after switching the workflow to the memcli CLI entrypoint.

title: Switch MemSpren skill/runtime docs to memcli CLI entrypoint
content: Updated the OpenClaw skill instructions and sync workflow to use the installed memcli command instead of uv run -m scripts.memcli. This makes the package behavior consistent with the intended open-source installation model, where memcli is provided as a console script and automation should not depend on repo-local module paths.

title: Implement state file pattern (partial) - Stage 0 working
content: Implemented shared state file pattern to work around Lobster's JSON path limitation. Created scripts/state.py helper with read/write/get_field methods. Updated check_cli.py and vault_diff_scanner.py to use state. Workflow now progresses through Stage 0 (pre-flight) successfully. Stops at extraction step (openclaw.invoke not available in test env). Remaining work: update all remaining scripts (task_inbox, extraction, parallel_refinement, entity_plan, entity_writes, metrics) to use state pattern.

title: Identify Lobster JSON path limitation + commit datetime fixes
content: Fixed all datetime.utcnow() deprecation warnings (replaced with datetime.now(UTC)). Discovered Lobster limitation: no support for $step.json.field nested access in workflow commands - only $step.json (entire object), $step.stdout, $step.approved/skipped supported. Workflow needs refactor to use state file pattern: scripts write to MEMORY_PATH/run/state.json, subsequent steps read from known paths. This is a Lobster core limitation, not a bug in our workflow design.

title: Fix Lobster workflow variable expansion and conditions
content: Fixed two critical Lobster workflow issues: (1) env: variable assignments don't expand LOBSTER_ARG_* references - must use them directly in run: commands. Removed env: section and replaced all $VAULT_PATH/$VAULT_NAME/$MEMORY_PATH with direct $LOBSTER_ARG_* references. (2) Lobster's when: clause only supports $step.approved|$step.skipped, not arbitrary JSON paths like $step.json.field. Removed early-exit conditional logic - downstream scripts handle empty buffers gracefully.
